core_obligations: Reduction to the nonzero case (proof lines 433-444): the author forms the span of those vectors whose tensor with the identity lies in the two-sided subspace, shows that its tensor product with the skew field is contained in it, and then argues that passing to the quotient produces a smaller configuration in which no nonzero vector has its constant tensor in the subspace, so it suffices to prove that a nonzero two-sided subspace meets the constants nontrivially.

Minimal expressions (proof lines 446-454): choosing a nonzero element of the subspace with a minimal number of nonzero tensor summands, one may multiply on the right so that the first coefficient is the identity; if there is only one summand the element is a constant tensor and the claim follows.

The commutator argument (proof lines 455-459): if there were more than one summand, commuting the element with an arbitrary element of the skew field produces a shorter nonzero element of the subspace by the two-sidedness assumption, so minimality forces every coefficient to commute with the whole skew field and hence, by centrality, to lie in the ground field, which makes the element a constant tensor and contradicts the assumption on the number of summands.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case where no nonzero constant tensor lies in the subspace by passing to a quotient.
Take an element of the subspace with the minimal number of tensor summands.
Commute it with an element of the skew field and use minimality to force all coefficients into the ground field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a two-sided subspace of the tensor product of a vector space with a central skew field is generated as a left module by the elements of the subspace that lie in the constants (statement lines 425-431). The proof is a complete argument: the span of the constant tensors occurring in the subspace is cut out and the configuration is reduced to the case where a nonzero two-sided subspace meets the constants trivially (proof lines 433-444); in that case an element with a minimal number of tensor summands is normalized (proof lines 446-454); and commuting that element with an arbitrary element of the skew field produces a shorter nonzero element unless every coefficient lies in the center of the skew field, which by centrality means the element was already a constant tensor, a contradiction (proof lines 455-459). The non-formal content is the reduction to the minimal expression and the commutator trick. The claim is H2.
